automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.

bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version

- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

{"command":"# From this, we see:
# - Keywords: package, func, if, for, switch, case are IsKeyword=true
# - Operators: many punctuation like (, ), {, }, :=, +, =, +=, ++, :, ; are IsOperator=true
# So IsOperator includes punctuation as well.

# So dupl likely distinguishes keywords (keeps them distinct) but normalizes operators and identifiers and literals? Let's test hypothesis:
# - If token.IsKeyword(): keep token as is (so if, for, switch, case, func, var, etc distinct)
# - Else if token == IDENT: map to generic IDENT token
# - Else if token is literal (INT, FLOAT, STRING, etc): map to generic LIT token
# - Else (operator): maybe map all operators to same token? Or keep some distinction?

# We observed operators like + vs - considered same, := vs = same, < vs > same, == vs != same. So operators are normalized to same token.

# What about "(" vs "{"? Are they considered same or distinct? Let's test.

cat <<'EOF' > /tmp/min/paren.go
package main
func f1() { a := 1 }
func f2() { a := (1) }
EOF
for t in 5 6 7 8 9 10; do printf "%2d: " $t; /workspace/executable -t $t /tmp/min/paren.go 2>&1 | head -n 1; done

cat <<'EOF' > /tmp/min/brace.go
package main
func f1() { a := 1 }
func f2() { a := func(){}() }
EOF
for t in 5 6 7 8 9 10 11 12; do printf "%2d: " $t; /workspace/executable -t $t /tmp/min/brace.go 2>&1 | head -n 1; done

# For paren test: f1 has a:=1, f2 has a:=(1). The extra parentheses would add "(" and ")" tokens. If "(" and ")" are normalized same as other operators, then still duplicate? Let's see.

# For brace test: f1 has a:=1, f2 has a:=func(){}() which includes extra braces and parentheses.

# Let's also test comma vs semicolon etc.

cat <<'EOF' > /tmp/min/comma.go
package main
func f1(a int) { println(a) }
func f2(a, b int) { println(a) }
EOF
for t in 5 6 7 8 9 10; do printf "%2d: " $t; /workspace/executable -t $t /tmp/min/comma.go 2>&1 | head -n 1; done

"}

  }

   for i:=1;i<len(occs);i++{
    if occs[i].pos < occs[i-1].pos+occs[i-1].length {
     overlap = true
     break
    }
   }
   if overlap {break}
  }
  if !overlap {
   filtered=append(filtered, g)
  }
 }

  l:=g[0].length

 for k,g := range grouped {

 }
